Stated Claim / Post Context:
Finalist group vying to be Chicago’s next top cop has decidedly homegrown flavor

The three finalists for the job of Chicago’s top cop — First Deputy Supt. Antoinette Ursitti, Chief Angel Novalez and Chief Christopher Papaioannou — are all longtime CPD leaders.

Actual Article Body:
eNewspaper

eNewspaper

Trending:

A key choice on police leadership now sits with Mayor Brandon Johnson, but a few things are certain.

The next superintendent of the Chicago Police Department more than likely lives on the Northwest Side and has been with the department for more than 25 years. They have worked assignments across the city, overseeing critical aspects of CPD’s day-to-day crime-fighting efforts, training curricula and reform efforts.

The three finalists for the job — First Deputy Superintendent Antoinette Ursitti, Chief Angel Novalez and Chief Christopher Papaioannou — are all longtime CPD leaders who fit that description, each promoted to their current position by the man they hope to supersede: retired Superintendent Larry Snelling.

“All three candidates understand the Chicago Police Department inside out, they understand the culture, and they understand our officers, and I think that means a lot to the rank-and-file as we’re searching for our next leader,” 10th Ward Ald. Peter Chico, a former CPD officer, told the Tribune Friday.

“I think Superintendent Snelling saw something in each of them and that’s why he made those promotions,” Chico added. “I think they all have their own skill set that will bode well if they are chosen.”

The 2026 search for the Police Department’s next leader certainly looks different from other recent iterations: There was no politicking on any one candidate’s behalf, and no applicant from outside CPD advanced to the final stage. The days of CPD being led by an out-of-state police chief or former federal agent appear to be over for now.

As recently as 2020, then-Mayor Lori Lightfoot tapped David Brown, the former chief of police in Dallas, to be superintendent. In that search, the other two finalists were a former CPD deputy chief and a now-former chief from Aurora.

“We’ve had outsiders in recent years and it hasn’t worked out,” 19th Ward Ald. Matt O’Shea told the Tribune on Friday.

“Larry Snelling was a strong leader, and Larry Snelling knows how to identify strong leaders,” he added. “If you see who he promoted into positions of leadership, they were cut from the same cloth as him: no nonsense, (he) stood behind the men and women under his command, and (he) held people accountable.”
